messages:
anya: Quick sync: engineering asked whether we can compress MVP timeline by 3 weeks if we scope down the v1 feature set. customer pilots want earlier availability.
 tom: what are the top candidate cuts? i assume dashboards, embeddings auto-ttl, and advanced quota UI are on the table?
 lucy: yes. realistic cuts: 1) defer embeddings cache tuning (keep basic cache), 2) defer per-route cost breakdown in console, 3) ship simplified model quantization profiles instead of full autotune.
 jason: which of those reduces platform dev work vs infra ops work? need to know how it shifts risk.
 lucy: deferring console cost metrics saves mostly front-end + product work. cache tuning is infra/infra-ml (ops & runtime) and is higher ROI for cost later, so cutting it helps timeline but increases token cost during pilot.
 mike: ops perspective: we can accept higher cost for a 2-week pilot if we have hard rate-limits and a fallback model variant. i.e., limit pilot to X reqs/day and auto-fallback if p99>800ms or error-rate>1%.
 anya: product ask: customers care about predictable latency and a rollback guarantee. can we commit to a playbook we can actually meet?
 kevin: yes. propose playbook: 1) Canary traffic ramp: 1%, 10%, 30% over 24-48h. 2) SLO gates: p99 <= 750ms, errors < 0.5%. 3) If gate fails, immediate rollback to safe-model; ops runbook triggers within 15 mins; broad rollback within 4 hours.
 jason: does fallback to safe-model preserve functionality? customers might see quality delta.
 lucy: safe-model is a slightly smaller quantized variant. functionality intact, some quality drop in edge cases. we should highlight that in pilot T&Cs.
 sarah-legal: flag: pilot contract must include a note about performance vs quality tradeoffs and an explicit rollback SLA. also need consent for temporary elevated logging if we enable deeper tracing during pilot.
 mike: agree. ops needs that elevated logging permission to debug regressions quickly.
 anya: decision proposal: Ship MVP earlier by deferring embeddings tuning and cost-by-route console; keep basic cache, add strict pilot rate-limits, implement canary ramp + SLO gates + fallback safe-model, and include rollback SLA and elevated-logging consent in pilot T&Cs. Approve?
 tom: approve pending a visibility plan for product/support so they know when pins/rollbacks happen.
 jason: approve. i'll own the customer-facing doc describing expected quality delta and rollback policy.
 lucy: engineering approves on the condition we don't reassign the runtime team mid-sprint. i'll post ETA for the canary automation (7 days).
 kevin: ops approves. i'll build the emergency toggle + automation: auto-fallback + telemetry hook for alerts. ETA 5 days.
 sarah-legal: legal approves the rollback SLA language; i'll send a draft clause for review today.
 deploy-bot: scheduled: pipeline "mvp/accelerate/canary-playbook" will run on 2026-09-02 01:00 UTC. status: pending.
 anya: action items: jason - draft customer pilot notice and quality/disclaimer doc (due Thu); lucy - canary automation ETA + PR (due Fri); kevin - emergency toggle + test (due Fri); mike - set pilot rate-limits and runbook steps (due Thu); sarah-legal - draft rollback SLA + logging consent (due Wed).
 tom: i'll update roadmap tracker to reflect deferred items to v1 and note the risk/mitigation column.
 anya: thanks all. if any blocker emerges, call it out here and i'll escalate. aim to finalize pilot T&C by COB Wed. :thumbsup:
